annotation.interpretation_a: Any MAX_STREAM_DATA frame, regardless of its content, must be retransmitted if it was the most recent one sent.
annotation.interpretation_b: Only MAX_STREAM_DATA frames that contained actual data (i.e., were not zero-length) must be retransmitted if they were the most recent one sent. A zero-length frame might signal the end of a stream and not require retransmission.
annotation.justification: The clause states that 'The most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA frame...MUST be retransmitted.' It doesn't clarify if this applies to all MAX_STREAM_DATA frames, including those with zero length, or only those carrying data. This missing constraint leads to two reasonable interpretations.
annotation.missing_information: The clause does not specify whether a zero-length MAX_STREAM_DATA frame also needs to be retransmitted. This affects implementation because a receiver might handle zero-length frames differently.
